intended: All four blocks sit on one farm in one summer, so a single rainfall record covers every case at once. The mid-passage facts state that rainfall in each block's season ran to roughly double the year before and that every block lay in open ground, taking rain as it fell, so the extra water reached every block whose yield was measured. Each block is compared against itself a season earlier rather than against an undripped block in the same season, so the rain and the drip line moved together and the 0.4 to 0.7 tonne gains cannot be attributed to the line. The population and completeness clauses in the same line describe a tally with no gap between the ground measured and the ground the claim covers, so the rainfall is the whole of the defect.
reported: Rainfall is an uncontrolled alternative cause that reaches every unit: "Rainfall in each block's season ran to roughly double the year before, and every block lay in open ground, taking rain as it fell." Doubled rainfall on open-ground maize plausibly produces the 0.4-0.7 t/ha gains on its own, and all four blocks are the same Hollow Ridge maize field fitted 3-6 June.

Doubled rainfall falling directly on open-ground maize blocks could produce the 0.4-0.7 t/ha gains regardless of the drip line.

intended: In cases one and three the comprehension score was recorded before the program began: 11 September precedes 6 December at Ashcombe Primary, and 24 April precedes 20 June at Halloway Junior. Half the evidence therefore describes gains that were already in place when the classes started the program, so it cannot be evidence for the program. The two remaining cases, Deerpark Academy and Marchfield Grange, are too few to establish the claim on their own.
reported: Two of the four classes have outcome dates that precede the start of the program: Ashcombe 'started the program 6 December' but scored higher 'by 11 September', and Halloway 'started the program 20 June' but scored higher 'by 24 April'. The other two (8 January / by 12 March; 6 July / by 21 August) run forward on short lags, so the gains in cases One and Three were measured before the program began.

intended: All four sections sit at Harlow in one autumn term, so a single change to the central syllabus covers every case at once. The mid-passage facts state that the central syllabus doubled coursework's share of the final grade against the previous year and that every section was marked to that central syllabus, so the heavier weighting applied to every section whose completion was measured. Each section is compared against itself a year earlier under the old share, so the kit and the doubled share moved together and the 6 to 11 point rises cannot be attributed to the kit. The population and completeness clauses in the same line describe a tally with no gap between the students counted and the students the claim covers, so the syllabus change is the whole of the defect.
reported: A named alternative cause reaches all four sections: 'The central syllabus doubled coursework's share of the final grade against the previous year, and every section was marked to that central syllabus.' Doubling coursework's weight is itself a reason completion would rise 6-11 points, and it applied to every unit measured, so the lab kit cannot be separated from it.

intended: The mid-passage line tallies the averages over the patients who were reassessed at the follow-up clinic, and the clause beside it records that a quarter of each intake missed that clinic. The claim is about the protocol restoring shoulder range of motion for the patients put on it, so the population is the whole intake and the register covers three quarters of it. Patients whose shoulders are not improving are the ones who stop turning up for reassessment, so the missing quarter is where the flat and negative results would sit, and the reported figures are an average over the patients who came back. The four intakes span four hospitals, four injury types, four seasons and four therapists, and the missed-clinic clause applies to each intake, so the same quarter is absent from every case rather than being covered by any of them.
reported: The abduction averages 'cover the patients who were reassessed at the follow-up clinic, and a quarter of each intake missed the follow-up clinic', so the 9-16 degree gains describe only the three quarters who came back, a narrower and plausibly better-recovering group than the intakes the claim is about.

(The corticosteroid confounder is closed off: injections "held level with the earlier quarter.")

intended: All four plots sit in the same backyard in the same summer, so one weather history covers every case at once. The mid-passage facts state that rainfall in each plot's season was the highest on record, roughly double the year before, and that every plot stood in the open, watered by rain alone, so that water reached every plot whose heights were taken. Each plot is compared against itself a year earlier rather than against an unfertilized plot in the same year, so the rain and the fertilizer moved together and the 8 to 13 cm gains cannot be attributed to the fertilizer. The population and completeness clauses in the same line describe a tally with no gap between the plants measured and the plants the claim covers, so the rainfall is the whole of the defect.
reported: Record rainfall is an untangled alternative cause that reaches every plot: 'Rainfall in each plot's season was the highest on record, roughly double the year before, and every plot stood in the open, watered by rain alone.' Double the water in all four plots fits the 8-13 cm gains at least as well as the fertilizer does.
